name: Breast cancer
summary: Cancer that starts in the breast. Finding it early gives people a much better chance of treatment.
signs: A new lump in the breast or underarm
Change in breast size or shape
prevention: Know what is normal for your body
Ask about screening from age 40, or earlier if your family has had breast cancer
See a health worker if you notice a new lump

name: Cervical cancer
summary: Cancer of the cervix. Screening and the HPV vaccine can prevent most cases.
signs: Bleeding after sex or between periods
prevention: HPV vaccine for girls and boys when offered
Regular screening (VIA or Pap) as advised locally

name: Prostate cancer
summary: Cancer of the prostate gland. It is more common in older men and can grow slowly.
signs: Getting up often at night to urinate
prevention: Talk to a health worker from age 50, or earlier with family history
Ask about a simple blood test (PSA) if offered

name: Liver cancer
summary: Cancer that starts in the liver. Hepatitis vaccination and avoiding aflatoxins help lower risk.
signs: Pain on the right side of the belly
prevention: Store grains and groundnuts dry to reduce mould
Limit alcohol and seek care for hepatitis

name: Colorectal cancer
summary: Cancer of the colon or rectum. Screening and early care save lives.
signs: A change in bowel habits that lasts
Belly pain or unexplained weight loss
prevention: Ask about screening if you are 50 or older, or have family history
